strings.item.seal.name: Damaged Seal
strings.item.seal.description: The number was stamped twice. Beneath the wear it reads C-17.
strings.item.timetable.name: Working Timetable
strings.item.timetable.description: Three wagons were rebooked without a destination station being named.
strings.item.ledger.name: Freight Ledger
strings.item.ledger.description: A new line bears the same code, C-17. The consignee has been blacked out.
strings.item.plan_a.name: Approved Plan
strings.item.plan_a.description: The public floor plan shows a closed-off service wing.
strings.item.plan_b.name: Archived Preliminary Design
strings.item.plan_b.description: In the earlier design, a corridor runs on behind the wall.
strings.item.emil_note.name: Emil’s Note
strings.item.emil_note.description: The archive number refers to a cross-border construction series: C-17.
strings.dlg.irina.01: The train came on time. The wagons in the papers didn’t come with it.
strings.dlg.irina.02: Three numbers. And a destination that’s on no public map.
strings.dlg.alexei.02: Give me the timetable and the seal. I’ll check it myself.
strings.dlg.irina.03: Then look twice. Once for the file, once for the people.
strings.dlg.irina.branch_a: I’ll tell you before I report anything.
strings.dlg.irina.branch_b: The less you know, the safer you might be.
strings.dlg.emil.01: There are the plans they build from. And the ones they file away.
strings.dlg.konrad.01: Both bear the same approval. That is impossible.
strings.dlg.emil.02: In an archive, the only impossible thing is what nobody is allowed to record.
strings.dlg.konrad.02: There’s a second wall here. A corridor carries on behind it.
strings.dlg.emil.03: The code C-17 isn’t a room. It’s a series of contracts.
strings.dlg.konrad.branch_a: I’ll keep a copy. The original stays here.
strings.dlg.konrad.branch_b: I shall make an official enquiry. There must be a memo somewhere.
strings.cinematic.a1_to_m1: The red code C-17 becomes a pencil note on a Berlin building plan.
strings.cinematic.hall_reveal: The Great Hall fills the horizon; below, a family waits outside a locked flat.
strings.cinematic.final: Two distant places. The same code. A peace whose files do not tally.
strings.world.a1.title: Karsk Loading Yard
strings.world.m1.title: Berlin Building Archive
strings.world.x1.title: Two Cities – One Document
strings.dlg.c3.cond_01: Hands off the seal, Engineer. Van four isn’t part of the train – only of the journey.
strings.dlg.c3.cond_03: A van with a key. And the key travels first class.
strings.dlg.c3.cond_05: At Kordon-17, on the Line. One a week. Sometimes from your side, sometimes from ours.
strings.dlg.c3.cond_07: Paper, says the weighbill. I count wagons, not files. It’s healthier – on both sides.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_01: Soviet delegation to counter two. Your papers, please. The Reich delegation is processed at counter one.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_02: I interpret for the Commission. He is asking the purpose of your journey.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_03: A technical assessment. The track connection at Kordon-17.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_04: There’s something else here: ‘Escort, courier van 4’. You said nothing about that.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_06: The note is bilingual. In Russian you are escorting freight. In German you are escorting files.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_07: The words are not my business. The stamp is.
strings.dlg.c3.ctrl_08: Welcome to Veltrava, Herr Morozov. Here everyone is a foreigner. It makes the work fair.
strings.dlg.c3.el_01: You read the note before the officer read it out. I saw you.
strings.dlg.c3.el_03: Then read Annex C twice. It exists in German, Russian and French. All three are binding.
strings.dlg.c3.el_04: And do all three say the same?
strings.dlg.c3.el_05: Almost. I note the places where they don’t. That is what the Commission pays me for.
strings.dlg.c3.el_07: My brother once signed a form. Nobody translated the small print for him. Since then I translate the small print.
strings.dlg.c3.el_09: On a list. – Go to your delegation, Herr Morozov. In Veltrava everyone listens in. The neutrals most closely of all.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_01: Adler. The delegation has been complete for twenty minutes – apart from you. The Commission does not wait for draughtsmen.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_02: They checked the luggage at the station, Director.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_03: The plans for Kordon-17 to the minutes office. Tomorrow you explain every drawing to the committee – slowly, clearly, no opinions.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_04: Frau Weiss of the Commission will put your terms into Russian. See to it that there are no misunderstandings.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_05: Herr Adler, a question first. Your plan names a ‘registration room’. What is registered there?
strings.dlg.c3.arr_06: Records. An archive room with sorting tables and card cabinets.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_07: The Russian version says ‘collection point’. One doesn’t say that of index cards.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_08: Translations differ. That is what you are for.
strings.dlg.c3.arr_09: That is what I am for. I’m writing it down. Booth two, if you’re looking for me.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_02: Nor yours. Soviet delegation, I take it – the badge.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_03: Technical assessor. I’m looking for Frau Weiss.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_04: She isn’t here. Neither is her logbook. Her coat is still hanging in the cloakroom downstairs.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_05: And you just happen to be standing in her booth. With a pencil in your hand.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_06: I am a draughtsman. I read what lies on desks.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_07: Three wagons are missing in Karsk. Their seal bore the same series as the papers here.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_08: In Berlin a corridor bears the same series. One that ought not to exist.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_10: C-17. – You are Russian, I am German. We were taught that one of us is lying.
strings.dlg.c3.meet_11: We were taught a lot. Not the same things. – Morozov. Karsk.

strings.item.c3_weighbill.name: Weighbill, Courier Van 4
strings.item.c3_weighbill.description: Load: “Files, Annex C”, 2410 kg. Seal C-17/44 with the Commission’s counter-seal. Consignee: Secretariat of the Commission.
strings.item.c3_departures.name: Special Run 23:40
strings.item.c3_departures.description: The departure board lists a non-stop train to Kordon-17 tonight, Platform 5. Under “Train class” it says only: empty run.
strings.item.c3_travel_order.name: Travel Order with Addendum
strings.item.c3_travel_order.description: Alexei’s travel order bears an addendum he knew nothing about: “Escort, courier van 4”. In Russian he escorts freight, in German files.
strings.item.c3_seating.name: Seating Plan, Opening Session
strings.item.c3_seating.description: A horseshoe table in the Great Chamber. The microphones are numbered clockwise from the chair; the Secretariat sits at a table of its own on the open side.
strings.item.c3_booth_log.name: Interpreter’s Log, Booth 2
strings.item.c3_booth_log.description: Elena’s log of the session: time, microphone, language. Beside paragraph four, her margin note: “RU: escorted persons – DE: escorted goods!”
strings.item.c3_carbon.name: Impression from Booth 2
strings.item.c3_carbon.description: Elena’s last note has pressed through onto her writing pad: “§ 4 – Persons. From the Secretariat, not from a delegation. Who supplied the text?” Her logbook is missing.
strings.item.c3_cut_seal.name: Cut Seal C-17/44
strings.item.c3_cut_seal.description: The crates from courier van 4 stand empty at the ramp. The seal still hangs on its wire – cut, not broken, with cutters someone had brought for the job.
strings.item.c3_night_book.name: Porter’s Night Book
strings.item.c3_night_book.description: “23:10 – Weiss, E. (Commission): logbook Booth 2 for filing.” Below: “23:25 – out.” Someone else wrote the second line. The lodge is empty; no coat hangs on the hook.
strings.item.c3_intake_book.name: Registry Intake Book, Series C-17
strings.item.c3_intake_book.description: Every Tuesday a courier van, sometimes from Karsk, sometimes from Berlin. Today, 09:52: van 4, seal C-17/44, 2410 kg “files”. Out 23:40, Platform 5: “Escorted goods, 14 pieces”. Russian column: 14 persons.
strings.item.c3_scarf.name: Elena’s Scarf
strings.item.c3_scarf.description: The wine-red scarf Elena wore at the Palace this morning hangs over the chair in front of drawer C-17. A bundle of cards is missing at the front – where they stood, there is no dust.
strings.item.c3_halves.name: Two Halves on One Table
strings.item.c3_halves.description: Alexei’s freight trail – weighbill, departure board, travel order, working timetable from Karsk – beside Konrad’s seating plan, interpreter’s log and impression. For the first time, everything lies on one table.
strings.item.c3_kordon_plan.name: Annex C, Sheet 7: Registration Room Kordon-17
strings.item.c3_kordon_plan.description: A room exactly on the Line: one door to the German hall, one to the Soviet, and between them a pass-through hatch. Revision c, in a different ink: “Waiting bench, 14 places”. Title block: drawn K. Adler.
strings.item.c3_file.name: File C-17 · Counterpart Offices
strings.item.c3_file.description: The Registry’s file on series C-17: requests from Berlin and from Karsk, carbons of the intake book, the escort list for the next special run. The cover is warm.
strings.item.c3_bolt.name: Bolted Ramp Door
strings.item.c3_bolt.description: The ramp door won’t give. Through the gap at the bottom: the bolt has been shot from outside, and fresh tracks in the snow lead to the gate.
strings.item.c3_cut_hose.name: Cut Fire Hose
strings.item.c3_cut_hose.description: The fire cabinet stands open, the hose cut through – clean, not torn. Whoever set the fire knew the building.
strings.item.c3_escort_list.name: Escort List, Tuesday 23:40
strings.item.c3_escort_list.description: The file has broken apart at the binding. On top, the list for the next special run, Tuesday, 23:40: column “Door West”, column “Door East”. Door East, third line: Iljin, P. A., b. 1935.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_01: Stop right there. – Oh. It’s you.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_03: Under the door, just after midnight. Written in German, with an E beneath it.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_04: Mine was in Russian. Same hand.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_05: She isn’t here. The lodge is empty; the light was already on when I came.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_06: Her name is in the night book, 23:10. At 23:25 someone wrote ‘out’ for her. With a different pen.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_07: And the crates outside on the ramp?
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_08: From van four. Empty, the seal cut. Whatever was inside is in here now.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_09: The Registry is the Secretariat. Every sheet the Commission produces passes through this building.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_10: And you? What are you looking for here, Adler?
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_11: Who supplied the text of paragraph four. And what became of my drawings.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_12: Where my wagons go. – You have light, I have papers. Let’s start.
strings.dlg.c3p2.night_13: At the sorting table. Touch nothing you cannot put back exactly as it was.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cmp_04: Seating plan, interpreter’s log, the impression from booth two.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cmp_05: Weighbill, departure board, my travel order. And the working timetable from Karsk.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cmp_06: Plus the intake book. Three columns, German, Russian, French – and every line has a number.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cmp_07: Then line by line. Your paper against mine.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_01: Sheet seven. Kordon-17, registration room. A room exactly on the Line.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_02: Two doors. One to your hall, one to ours. And a hatch in between.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_03: A pass-through hatch. For card boxes – so the legend says.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_04: And a bench with fourteen places. Card boxes don’t sit.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_05: Revision c. The bench was added later, in a different ink.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_06: I thought your people were taking our wagons.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_07: And I thought your people wanted our corridors.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_08: They swap. Sometimes from your side, sometimes from ours – that’s what the conductor said.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_09: Then the party to the contract is not your country. It is the offices that keep the lists – yours and ours.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_10: Ours is called the Transport Department. Whoever comes back through it doesn’t come home.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_11: Ours is called the Registration Office. What comes after registration, nobody calls by its name. Nor do I.
strings.dlg.c3p2.par_12: Who draws a room like that, Adler?
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_01: The ramp is shut. Bolted from outside.
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_02: Here – the old spa-house plan, 1909. Basement: coal cellar. A chute leads up into the service yard.
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_03: The iron door behind the desk. With the year on it.
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_04: The desk is oak. Neither of us can shift it alone.
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_05: Then not alone. Take the file – I need my hands.
strings.dlg.c3p2.smk_06: Sheet seven is still on the wall. – Let it burn.
strings.dlg.c3p2.dsk_01: On three. You push, I pull.
strings.dlg.c3p2.dsk_02: I draw desks, Morozov. I don’t push them.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cht_01: The door’s jammed. I’ll hold it. First the file, then you.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cht_02: And who holds the door when you go last?
strings.dlg.c3p2.cht_03: Nobody. That’s why I go last.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cht_04: That is not an engineer’s solution.
strings.dlg.c3p2.cht_05: It is. One from Karsk. – Go, Adler!
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_01: The binding has burnt through. The file is falling apart by itself.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_02: German sheets, Russian sheets. As if to order.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_03: You’ve been reading the Russian column for a minute. What does it say?
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_04: Third line. Iljin, Pjotr Andrejewitsch. As boys we put kopecks on the rails in Karsk.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_05: He’s on the list for Tuesday.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_06: He crossed the Line in 1957. He’s lived here ever since, in Veltrava. So I thought.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_07: There are names in the German column too. I don’t know any of them. Not yet.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_08: Fourteen pieces at 23:40. At 23:25 someone wrote ‘out’ for Elena.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_09: You think she was on that train.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_10: I no longer believe anything written on one paper. Only what two papers say together.
strings.dlg.c3p2.snw_11: Any moment the guards will search everyone with soot on their face. We won’t get far with the whole file.

strings.obj.c3c_crates: Look at the crates on the ramp.
strings.obj.c3c_night_book: Read the night book in the porter’s lodge.
strings.obj.c3c_konrad: Follow the light between the filing cabinets.
strings.obj.c3d_drawer: Look at the open drawer C-17.
strings.obj.c3d_check: Check record against record: which entry belongs to which paper?
strings.obj.c3d_plan: Find Sheet 7 of Annex C on the plan wall.
strings.obj.c3d_choice: Decide what you tell him about Sheet 7.
strings.obj.c3e_file: Take File C-17 from the sorting table.
strings.obj.c3e_ramp: Try to get out through the ramp door.
strings.obj.c3e_konrad: Follow Adler’s voice to the porter’s lodge.
strings.obj.c3f_hose: Get the fire hose from the fire cabinet.
strings.obj.c3f_desk: Push the desk off the coal chute with Morozov.
strings.obj.c3f_chute: Climb into the chute with the file.
strings.obj.c3g_file: See what is left of the file.
strings.obj.c3g_choice: Decide how the two of you split the file.
strings.choice.c3d.admit_plan: Tell him that Sheet 7 is your drawing
strings.choice.c3d.pocket_plan: Pocket Sheet 7 and say: ‘An office in Berlin.’
strings.choice.c3g.split_by_language: Split by language: you take the Russian sheets, he takes the German
strings.choice.c3g.swap_halves: Split crosswise: he takes the Russian sheets with Pjotr’s name, you the German
strings.choice.c3g.hide_for_elena: Put the list in Elena’s coat – cloakroom, ticket 27 – and split the rest by language

strings.obj.c4a_lev: Talk to Lev Sokolov at his desk.
strings.obj.c4a_book: Read the ‘Approved’ column in the January ledger.
strings.obj.c4a_carbon: Hold Lev’s carbons up to the lamp.
strings.obj.c4a_tunnel: Ask Lev where the wagons went.
strings.obj.c4a_door: Open the iron door to the service tunnel.
strings.obj.c4b_notice: Read the notice on the door of number nine.
strings.obj.c4b_marta: Talk to the driver of the 74.
strings.obj.c4b_routes: Lay Marta’s route map over the site plan in the light of the timetable case.
strings.obj.c4b_column: Look at the advertising column by the loop.
strings.obj.c4b_ilse: Tell Marta what lies beneath her loop.
strings.obj.c4b_crates: Look at the crates by the loading hatch.
strings.obj.c4c_card: Read the index card on the table in the platelayers’ hut.
strings.obj.c4c_stencils: Look at the paint stand with the stencils.
strings.obj.c4c_numbers: Find out which numbers this wagon has carried.
strings.obj.c4d_drawer: Find the Süd 8 drawer in the card index.
strings.obj.c4d_plan: Look at the ventilation plan on the wall.
strings.obj.c4d_tube: Read what came by pneumatic post.
strings.obj.c4d_registrar: Ask at the counter for the Lindner file.
strings.obj.c4d_choice: Decide whether to give Marta’s name.
strings.choice.c4d.name_marta: Give Marta Vogel’s name – the Lindner file would be evidence with signatures, before Tuesday
strings.choice.c4d.protect_marta: Give no name – ‘I heard it on the street.’
strings.item.c4_book_gap.name: Gap on the Shelf
strings.item.c4_book_gap.description: Three volumes are missing from the shelf of freight ledgers: January 1964, first to third ten-day period. On the empty board lies a slip in Lev’s hand: “With L. S. – for review.”
strings.item.c4_cut_signatures.name: January Ledger, “Approved” Column
strings.item.c4_cut_signatures.description: On the three rebookings of 14, 21 and 28 January the signature has been cut out – cleanly, with a blade. Beside each, the same note: “Dept. T – verbal”.
strings.item.c4_carbon.name: Carbons with Pressure Marks
strings.item.c4_carbon.description: Lev keeps the carbon of every waybill. Against the lamp, what was cut out above shows through: “Ju. Archipov, Colonel, Transport Department” – three times the same hand.
strings.item.c4_tunnel_plan.name: Plan of Service Tunnel 3, 1941
strings.item.c4_tunnel_plan.description: An air-raid plan from 1941, mounted on linen. The tunnel runs beneath the whole goods yard and ends at a track with no number. Someone has traced the route in pencil.
strings.item.c4_fresh_tracks.name: Tracks behind the Iron Door
strings.item.c4_fresh_tracks.description: The rails in the tunnel are polished bright, the dust beside them trampled. On the threshold, a drop of red-brown paint, still soft.
strings.item.c4_notice.name: Eviction Notice No. 9 with Site Plan
strings.item.c4_notice.description: The January notice, with a fresh addendum below: “Household dissolved. Case passed to South Branch.” Pinned to it, site plan Süd 8 with three shafts, S 1 to S 3. Title block: drawn K. A.
strings.item.c4_route_board.name: Marta’s Route Map, Route 74
strings.item.c4_route_board.description: On tracing paper from the depot: Route 74 as it ran in autumn, and three diversions – October, December, January. Drawn in the direction of travel, not north-up.
strings.item.c4_shaft.name: Advertising Column S 2
strings.item.c4_shaft.description: Warm air rises from the grille at the foot of the column, in the middle of the frost. Behind the posters, a steel door: “Ventilation Structure S 2 – Branch Office Staff Only”.
strings.item.c4_card_de.name: Index Card No. 0417, German Half
strings.item.c4_card_de.description: Fallen into the snow from a burst crate: “Lindner, Anna, née Kowalenko, b. 1926 Kharkov. Note C-17: Repatriation East. Hand-over Kordon-17, Door East, courier van C-17/45, Tue 18.2., 23:40.” Below: “Child Ilse, 8 – whereabouts unknown.” A perforation on the right; the other half is missing.
strings.item.c4_card_ru.name: Index Card No. 0417, Russian Half
strings.item.c4_card_ru.description: In the box “C-17/45 – accept” on the table in the platelayers’ hut: “Kowalenko, Anna Petrowna, 1926, Kharkov. Taken to Germany in 1942. Returnee. Onward: Karsk filtration point.” A perforation on the left. Alexei copies the card and puts it back.
strings.item.c4_stencils.name: Stencils at the Paint Stand
strings.item.c4_stencils.description: Tin stencils in two alphabets, sorted by run: C-17/41 to /44, worn. C-17/45 is still stuck to the board, wet. Beside it a bucket of red-brown, the colour of every goods wagon.
strings.item.c4_wagon_inside.name: Wagon 24 318, Inside
strings.item.c4_wagon_inside.description: Two benches of rough planks, a stovepipe hole in the roof, a bucket. Scratched into the wall: names in two scripts and a date, 21.1. Below, smaller: “We are fourteen.”
strings.item.c4_drawer_s8.name: Drawer Süd 8
strings.item.c4_drawer_s8.description: One card for each cleared household in section Süd 8 of Route 74, 212 in all. 37 of them carry a red tab – C-17. All 37 are missing their right half.
strings.item.c4_annex_plan.name: Ventilation Plan, South Branch
strings.item.c4_annex_plan.description: Framed behind glass: ventilation plan, South Branch, 1961, sheet 3. Three shafts, above them three blocks of houses, hatched in pencil: “to be vacated”. Title block: drawn K. Adler.
strings.item.c4_tube_slip.name: State Police Pneumatic Slip
strings.item.c4_tube_slip.description: A slip in the capsule. Sender: State Police office, Kommissar Wendt. “By Monday: all C-17 households Süd 8, whereabouts of the children. Informants by name.”
strings.dlg.c4.lev_01: Nobody comes to the archive at this hour, Morozov. Only someone who doesn’t want to be in the duty book.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_02: The January freight ledgers. There’s a gap on the shelf.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_03: I am the gap. The ledgers are under my elbow. Whoever wants them has to get past me.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_04: Three wagons in January, rebooked with no destination. They arrived in Veltrava – as C-17. I carry the list with me.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_05: You were in Veltrava and came back. Not everyone who crosses the Line manages that.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_07: The ‘Approved’ column. Read it yourself. I say nothing that can be quoted later.
strings.dlg.c4.lev_08: Then I read, and you keep quiet. We’re both good at that.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_01: Archipov. Colonel, Transport Department. Three times the same hand.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_02: You read that, not I. I only keep carbons. Someone has to keep the second copy.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_03: The wagons never ran on the main line. They’re missing from the signal box register. I checked.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_04: Because they run underneath. Service tunnel three, built in forty-one against air raids. It runs under the whole goods yard.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_06: To a track that’s on no plan. That’s where the wagons get new numbers. – Here, the old tunnel plan.
strings.dlg.c4.tun_07: Why are you giving me this?
strings.dlg.c4.tun_08: Because I’m old and you’re not. And because my name will be on no paper, Morozov. None.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_01: The 74 doesn’t go for seven minutes, sir. And it’s no warmer inside.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_02: I don’t want to ride. I am a draughtsman at the General Building Office. This loop here is new.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_03: The third since October. Every time they clear a block, I drive a new curve round it.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_04: Building works. For the axis, so the notice says.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_05: Building works at three in the morning? With lorries that aren’t from any site? I drive the first tram. I see who gets taken.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_07: Number nine. The Lindners. Paul was a fitter at our depot. Anna came from Kharkov in forty-two, on a transport.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_08: I saw the family. In January, at the parade. They were standing outside their own door.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_09: On the third they took Anna. ‘Clarification of citizenship.’ Paul they transferred to the depot in Stettin.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_11: What child? – You ask a lot for a man who only draws.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_12: I drew the site plan for these clearances. Süd 8. I want to know what for.
strings.dlg.c4.mar_13: Then take this. My route as it ran in autumn, and as it runs today. See for yourself, Mister Draughtsman.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_01: Your three diversions lie exactly over three shafts. There is an office under this loop.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_02: An office. And so that it gets air, they cleared out number nine.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_03: And the people’s files went down there with them. ‘Case passed to South Branch’, says the notice.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_04: Then they know down there that the Lindners have a daughter.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_05: The girl on your tram. Back seat, satchel on her lap – she never lets go of it.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_06: Ilse. Eight. Officially she’s with an aunt in Stettin. In fact she sleeps at mine, and rides with me in the mornings.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_08: The teacher knows. A Fräulein Adler. She lets Ilse into the classroom before lessons, because of the cold.
strings.dlg.c4.ils_12: Then you know now what’s at stake. Whatever you find down there, I want to hear it. My name, nobody down there hears.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_01: Fourteen, scratched with a nail. So that someone reads it. – I know boards like these, Morozov.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_03: Fifty-three, after the armistice. Prisoner exchange on the Line. ‘Homecomers’ was chalked on the wagon.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_05: To Karsk. Filtration point, track nine. Whoever spent twelve years with the Germans must explain why he’s still alive.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_06: The card names the same place. Karsk filtration point. For Anna Kowalenko.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_07: The Germans took her in forty-two. Now we fetch her back – and ask her why she went with them.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_08: On Tuesday. In this wagon. And Pjotr with her.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_09: Enough with the names, Morozov. Names are what they collect up there.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_10: Then I’ll collect numbers. One wagon, four numbers since January. That can be counted, Lev.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_11: Counted. And who will you show it to? – Go, before the shift comes. On Sundays they start painting at eight.
strings.dlg.c4.sid_12: I’m going. And I’ll be back before Tuesday.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_01: South Branch, Enquiries and Verification. You’re early, Herr …?
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_02: Adler, General Building Office. Ventilation survey, sheet three. For the shaft planning I require a household file.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_03: Adler. Ventilation, sheet three – your name is on our plan on the wall. Which file?
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_04: Lindner, house number nine, Süd 8. I need to know who lived there. Because of the shaft wall.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_05: Lindner. Red tab, C-17. The file is complete, except for the child. Ilse, eight years old. Whereabouts unknown.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_06: For the shaft planning the occupancy will suffice. Who moved out, and when.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_07: C-17 files I release only in exchange for an informant. A resident who confirms the occupancy.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_09: Then give me her name. Whoever told you about the Lindners also knows where the child is.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_10: The child is of no interest to the General Building Office.
strings.dlg.c4.cnt_11: But to us, Herr Adler. Name and address, here on the form. There must be order – even down here.
strings.world.c4e.title: Karsk Locomotive Depot, Coal Bunker
strings.world.c4f.title: Ostbahnhof, Corridor Platform – Berlin
strings.world.c4g.title: Karsk Locomotive Depot, Show Side and Platform 1

strings.obj.c4e_order: Read the order in the window of the dispatcher’s hut.
strings.obj.c4e_list: Look at the list by the coal bunker.
strings.obj.c4e_maria: Talk to the woman in the green headscarf.
strings.obj.c4e_notice: Read the notice on the back door of the engine shed.
strings.obj.c4f_board: Read the departure board on the Corridor platform.
strings.obj.c4f_marta: Talk to Marta Vogel at the buffet.
strings.obj.c4f_courier: Look at the wagons behind the engine.
strings.obj.c4f_ekdahl: Talk to Nils Ekdahl by the dining car.
strings.obj.c4f_book: Put the card half into Ekdahl’s guidebook.
strings.obj.c4g_ekdahl: Show the Swedish journalist your signal.
strings.obj.c4g_lev: Lev is waiting in the sand-drying shed.
strings.obj.c4g_halves: Fit the two halves of card 0417 together.
strings.obj.c4g_card: Look at the whole card under the lamp.
strings.obj.c4g_choice: Decide what Ekdahl takes with him tonight.
strings.obj.c4h_gate: Read the notice in the archway.
strings.obj.c4h_hanna: Talk to Hanna in the courtyard.
strings.obj.c4h_cards: Look at the household card index in the lodge window.
strings.obj.c4h_house: Find a way for Ilse through house 14 that no card knows about.
strings.obj.c4h_wendt: Go to the men in the archway.
strings.item.c4_special_order.name: Order: Special Run C-17/45
strings.item.c4_special_order.description: A carbon in the window of the dispatcher’s hut: ‘Karsk Locomotive Depot provides one engine and one crew for special run C-17/45 on Tuesday, 18.2. Dep. transfer siding 19:40 local time, arr. Kordon-17 23:40 Corridor time. Wagon 24 318. Escort: Dept. T. The crew keeps silent.’ Below, in Irina’s pencil: ‘Who?’
strings.item.c4_work_list.name: Work List, Column 4
strings.item.c4_work_list.description: On the post of the coal bunker, under cellophane: ‘Column 4. Admitted 22.1.1964. Until screening is complete.’ Eleven names. In the margin, three notes in pencil: ‘Lena, 4, and Miron, 6 – Children’s Home No. 2’ and ‘Wilhelm S. – Special Settlement North’. Eleven and three make fourteen.
strings.item.c4_press_notice.name: Notice: Press Visit
strings.item.c4_press_notice.description: On the back door of the engine shed, with the depot management’s stamp: ‘Tuesday, 18.2., 17:30: visit by a representative of the Swedish press. To be shown: the restored line signal (Eng. A. Morozov), the model brigade, the canteen. Column 4 on this day: back yard, behind the tarpaulin.’
strings.item.c4_departures_east.name: Departure Board, Platform K
strings.item.c4_departures_east.description: ‘D 303 Berlin Ost – Kordon-17 – Karsk, dep. 21:10, Platform K.’ Below it a freshly painted sign: ‘Tuesday: special train to Kordon-17 with special wagon, dep. 15:30. Platform K closed from 15:00.’ A train due at the Line at 23:40.
strings.item.c4_courier_seals.name: Courier Van and Green Wagon
strings.item.c4_courier_seals.description: Behind the engine, a courier van with no windows. On the door, two lead seals, one German, one Soviet, both stamped ‘C-17’. On the next track, a green wagon with barred hatches. Chalked on the door: ‘Tue – Kordon’.
strings.item.c4_konrad_tracing.name: Konrad’s Tracing of Sheet 7
strings.item.c4_konrad_tracing.description: On tracing paper, from memory and with the ruler from his coat pocket: the room at Kordon-17, Door West, Door East, the pass-through hatch, the waiting bench for fourteen. On the back, in block capitals: ‘MOROZOV – 0417 – TUE 23:40 – DOOR EAST’. It lies with the German half of the card in Ekdahl’s guidebook, page 212.
strings.item.c4_guidebook.name: Ekdahl’s Guidebook, Page 212
strings.item.c4_guidebook.description: A Swedish guidebook from 1938, chapter ‘Karsk – Station and Depot’. Between the pages, the German half of card 0417, slipped in upside down, and a tracing: the room at Kordon-17, Door West, Door East, the waiting bench for fourteen. On the back, in block capitals: ‘MOROZOV – 0417 – TUE 23:40 – DOOR EAST’.
strings.item.c4_card_ru_original.name: Card 0417, Russian Half (Original)
strings.item.c4_card_ru_original.description: From the box ‘C-17/45 – accept’, borrowed for one hour: ‘Kowalenko, Anna Petrowna, 1926, Kharkov. Returnee. Onward: Karsk filtration point.’ Stamp: ‘Accept’. The perforation on the left, above it half a round stamp. By half past seven it must be back in the box.
strings.item.c4_card_whole.name: Card 0417, Whole
strings.item.c4_card_whole.description: The teeth of the perforation interlock. Left, in German: ‘Lindner, Anna, née Kowalenko … Note C-17: Repatriation East. Hand-over Kordon-17, Door East.’ Right, in Russian: ‘Kowalenko, Anna Petrowna … Accept … Onward: Karsk filtration point.’ Across the cut runs a round stamp, ‘C-17’, half in German, half in Russian script. It closes. Ekdahl takes two photographs.
strings.item.c4_house_notice.name: Notice in the Archway
strings.item.c4_house_notice.description: ‘Notice from the block wardens: all households are to hold themselves ready on Tuesday from 22:00 for inspection of the household card index. Children are to be presented.’ Below, with a drawing pin: ‘Construction section Süd 9 – Kolonnenstraße 12 to 18 – site plan’, the houses hatched. Title block: drawn K. A.
strings.item.c4_house_cards.name: Household Card Index, Kolonnenstraße 14
strings.item.c4_house_cards.description: A wooden box in the lodge window, one card per flat, in Kuhnert’s hand. Side wing 3: ‘Adler, Hanna, teacher, 1 pers.’ Side wing 2: ‘Pohl, Gertrud, widow – reports reliably’. Lodge: ‘Kuhnert, Erwin and Frieda – window on the courtyard’. Rear building 3: ‘empty, relocated 10/63’. Archway: ‘from 22:00 block warden’. Attic: ‘wash day Tue: open’. Last, with no household card: ‘Pietsch shoemaker’s, basement – trade’.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_01: You’ve read the order. An engine and a crew for a wagon that runs in no book.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_03: I have seven drivers. Each has children or a mother or a file. I’m sending nobody.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_05: Then Department T sends one. And under my name they write ‘crew refused’.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_06: The people at the coal bunker. Since when have they been shovelling here?
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_07: Since the twenty-second of January. Column four. They shovel coal for the trains that brought them here.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_09: Don’t ask me. Ask the woman in the green headscarf. She talks when the guard goes for tea.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_iri_10: And tomorrow at half past five a Swede from the newspaper is coming. You’re to show him your signal. Shave.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_01: You’re no guard. Guards don’t carry tool bags, and they don’t look you in the eye.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_02: Engineer. I count wagons that are in no book. One was called 24 318.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_03: Then you’ve seen our benches. And the hole for the stovepipe.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_04: ‘We are fourteen.’ It was in the wall, scratched with a nail.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_05: That was me. Maria Gorelowa. The children sat by the stove, Lena and Miron. Wilhelm made sure they didn’t touch the hot metal.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_07: The children in Children’s Home Number Two. Wilhelm in a special settlement in the north. He’s a German from the Black Sea – that’s enough.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_09: I shovel until the screening is done. Every day the same question: why did you go with them? Why are you still alive?
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_10: How did they find you in Veltrava?
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_11: Not me. My card. It got here before me; a man stood at the door, comparing. First comes the card, then the person.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_12: On Tuesday the next wagon comes. A woman from Berlin, Anna Kowalenko. And a friend of mine.
strings.dlg.c4p2.e_mar_13: Then tell someone who’s allowed to write it down. Nobody here believes us. They only question us.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_01: There you are, Herr Adler. Punctual as a timetable.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_03: Last night a man from the authorities was at the depot, asking questions.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_05: This morning I had a different route.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_06: What do you know about tomorrow?
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_07: Tomorrow evening they take the households with the red tab. The children too, says a colleague whose husband drives at the Ring.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_09: To their mothers, they say. ‘Family reunification.’ Ilse can’t sleep at mine tomorrow. They’ll look there first.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_10: Hanna. Kolonnenstraße fourteen. A house full of people who know her – and one who keeps cards.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_mar_11: Then I’ll bring Ilse to your sister tomorrow evening. And you, Mister Draughtsman, find out where that train goes.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_01: Herr Adler. You telephoned and said nothing. On the telephone that is the politest way to talk.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_03: A press tour, ‘The First Winter of the Accord’. They’ll show me a depot, a canteen and an engineer who repaired a signal.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_05: Morozov. It’s in the programme, with an exclamation mark. Why?
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_06: In Veltrava you said: if I ever draw something that isn’t right. I have drawn it. And he has the other half.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_07: At Kordon-17 they’ll search my luggage. And the gentleman at the news-stand has been reading the same page for twenty minutes.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_08: Nobody searches your guidebook. Every traveller reads it aloud.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_09: Page two hundred and twelve, ‘Karsk – Station and Depot’. Put it there. I won’t read it until after the border.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_10: You also said: a newspaper doesn’t stop a train.
strings.dlg.c4p2.f_ekd_11: No. But it records that the train ran. And sometimes someone stands beside it and counts along.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_01: So this is the signal that went green again in January. Your press office is very proud of you, Engineer.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_02: A signal is green when the line is clear. It says nothing more.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_03: My minder wishes me to write ‘reconstruction’. I shall. – Do you have a guidebook to Karsk?
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_04: No. Why would I? I live here.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_05: Then I’ll lend you mine. Page two hundred and twelve is especially thorough. A draughtsman in Berlin recommended it to me.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_07: He says you collect numbers. He collects rooms. I collect bystanders.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_08: Behind that tarpaulin, Column four is shovelling. Nobody writes them down.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_09: I saw the tarpaulin. When it moved, my minder showed me the canteen.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_ekd_10: Stay for the evening train. I’ll bring the book back before it leaves.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_01: One hour, Morozov. At half past seven the escort collects the box. Then the card is back in it – or I’m lying somewhere else.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_03: The right half, ‘accept’. And you have the left? From Berlin?
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_04: In a Swedish guidebook, page two hundred and twelve. A German put it there.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_05: A German, a Swede and a Russian at one table. In the old days they called that a commission.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_06: Your carbons, Lev. Archipov’s hand. The Swede goes west tonight.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_07: With them it’s a file. Without them it’s two half cards and a guidebook.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_08: I gave you my word. Your name on no paper.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_09: My name is on every carbon I ever kept. Invisible. Whoever prints them makes it legible.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_10: Take them if you must. I won’t ask what you did with them. I’ll find out.
strings.dlg.c4p2.g_lev_11: The card first. Then we’ll see what it weighs.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_01: You’re late, Konrad. Marta brought her at nine, with a bag of apples.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_03: Upstairs, at the kitchen table. She’s drawing houses with lit windows. That’s how you do it, she says, when everyone’s home.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_05: Inspection from ten p.m., children to be presented. And under it your plan. Twelve to eighteen, hatched. Us.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_06: Hanna, it is a site plan. Construction sections are registered long before –
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_07: Later, Konrad. There’s no child on the card for my flat. If they find Ilse there, tomorrow there’ll be one – with my name beside it.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_09: The box is in the lodge window. He’s waiting in the archway for the gentlemen; his wife is listening to the radio.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_10: Then I shall read what he knows. And look for what he doesn’t.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_11: You know houses. You draw them before they’re emptied. Find a place in this one that nobody has drawn.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_han_12: Put her coat on her. And leave your light on – so that everyone upstairs is home.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_01: Herr Adler, General Building Office. We haven’t met, but I know your handwriting.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_03: At half past eleven, in a house you hatched yourself. You are a thorough man.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_04: The planning provides for surveys of the existing buildings.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_05: Does a child named Ilse Lindner live here? Eight years old, a satchel she never lets go of?
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_06: There is none in the card index. Ask Herr Kuhnert.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_07: House fourteen, no child registered, Kommissar. Side wing, rear building, all ticked off. All in order.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_08: All in order. Then we climbed the stairs for nothing. It happens.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_10: Twenty-three forty. At this hour there’s always a train running somewhere.
strings.dlg.c4p2.h_wen_11: We’ll see each other again, Herr Adler. On Tuesdays we are always out and about.
strings.choice.c4g.publish_now: Give Ekdahl everything – the film, Lev’s carbons, the Column four list – so that he stands at Door East at 23:40
strings.choice.c4g.protect_first: Keep the film and give Ekdahl only the numbers – first Lev, Maria and Konrad’s people must get out of the line of fire
